searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase one — chesed: every plausible long render architecture the awtsmoos is beyond queue and codec, yet awtsmoos.com lets each frame enter a finite vessel without blocking the river's flow. candidate causes of the frame 12 stall mediabunny internal encoder queue reaches its own high water mark and add() awaits a dequeue event that is never wired. our shared wrapper queues frames but never starts/continues processframequeue after the first drain cycle. the worker closes imagebitmaps too late and backpressure is actually gpu resource exhaustion. mediabunny videosamplesource.add() requires sequential timestamps but a floating point boundary near frame 12 exposes validation. worker request acknowledgement is emitted before encoding finishes, hiding a later encoder failure until queue saturation. offscreencanvas or videoframe lifetime prevents more than a small number of outstanding samples. maxcacheframes is 8 but another queue threshold around 12 produces a deadlock between wrapper queue and codec queue. the full soundtrack buffer memory plus encoded video queue leaves insufficient memory for continued frame production. the browser target remains alive but the worker has thrown an exception that is not routed as fatal error. candidate repairs a. add explicit mediabunny queue drain promise and wait only when encoder queue crosses a threshold. b. encode synchronously one frame at a time and acknowledge only after mediabunny has accepted/drained it. c. use bounded batches: 4–8 frames, await drain, continue. d. add flushvideo() checkpoints every scene or n frames. e. chunk the movie into independent scene group mp4 fragments, then concatenate/remux. f. separate audio and video rendering completely, mux only after both artifacts exist. g. fall back to ffmpeg based image sequence encoding for long canonical proof while preserving webcodecs for browser preview. h. build a resumable render job layer above both webcodecs and ffmpeg. chosen direction criteria first repair the existing webcodecs path with evidence and bounded backpressure because the 3 second proof already validates its codec/mux result. then, after full 180 second proof, add chunk/resume as architecture rather than hiding the immediate defect behind a different encoder.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he phase two — gevurah: critique and failure guards the awtsmoos gives limitless light, while awtsmoos.com demands a vessel that never calls a silent hang success. 1. never merely increase queue sizes; that delays the same failure and increases memory risk. 2. never add arbitrary sleeps as the backpressure mechanism. 3. never swallow worker errors while awaiting frame acknowledgement. 4. every frame request must eventually resolve, reject, or time out with stage/index evidence. 5. avoid modifying canonical renderer semantics while fixing encoder flow. 6. do not replace the proven mp4 worker with ffmpeg until the actual defect is understood. 7. if a shared video helper is touched, rewrite the whole file and split dense responsibilities rather than partial patching. 8. keep browser worker source below 120 lines by extracting queue/drain helpers. 9. release/close imagebitmap and videoframe resources deterministically. 10. report queue depth, frame index, timestamp, and stage at least at coarse intervals. 11. long render test must exceed the encoder queue threshold; 3 seconds at 12fps is already enough but a 30 second fixture is stronger. 12. full proof must use the canonical 180 second movie, not a synthetic pattern. 13. full output must be independently probed by ffprobe. 14. frame witnesses must be derived from the actual mp4, not directly from the canonical renderer. 15. mobile ui proof must include actual interaction and console inspection. 16. existing green node tests remain required after every source repair. 17. do not rewrite unrelated peer files in the dirty shared workspace. 18. fresh hash every existing file immediately before full rewrite. 19. refactor over 120 neighbors only after their importers are traced. 20. completion requires stale plan/evidence artifacts to be reconciled with reality.

searchText: b"h boruch hashem blessed is he runtime discovery — frame six reveals flush reuse failure the awtsmoos renews every instant and exposes what yesterday's abstraction concealed; awtsmoos.com now has direct proof that one long lived browser videoencoder cannot be trusted across repeated drains in this worker vessel. direct evidence fresh no cache runtime loaded the rewritten workersession, framepump, requestbroker, and custom avc registration. mediabunny's stock native encoder stalled at queue depth four. the first custom strategy flushed the native encoder every three submitted frames. runtime advanced from the previous hard wall at frame four to five completed frames. frame six triggered the second flush on the same native videoencoder. the request broker then produced an explicit 30 second timeout: frame frame accepted ... frame=6, total=360, seconds=0.417. conclusion the fragile unit is the lifetime of a single browser videoencoder across repeated flush cycles. the next source strategy must not depend on a second flush succeeding on the same native encoder. revised design 1. mediabunny keeps ownership of mp4 muxing and its customvideoencoder extension contract. 2. one custom encoder object may live for the track, but it owns a sequence of short lived native videoencoder segments. 3. each native encoder receives at most three frames. 4. the first frame after native encoder creation is always forced keyframe, preserving decode independence across encoder restarts. 5. at three frames: flush exactly once, close, discard, and create a fresh native encoder for the next sample. 6. mediabunny final flush() only drains the currently active partial segment, again at most once for that native encoder. 7. every emitted packet still flows through mediabunny's encodedpacket.fromencodedchunk() and muxer callbacks. 8. regression tests must prove two segments create two native encoders, each flushed once, with a forced keyframe at each segment boundary. next action rewrite the custom avc adapter and its regression test around one flush per native encoder segmentation, then rerun the complete focused suite before browser proof.
